# Migrate deployment from AWS CodePipeline to GitHub Actions

## Context

Deployment today runs through a self-mutating CDK Pipeline (`RSSPipelineStack`) that
watches `eamonmason/rss-email@main` via a CodeConnections connection, synths in
CodeBuild (pulling config from SSM Parameter Store), and deploys the app stack through
a CDK Stage named `cd` — producing the CloudFormation stack **`cd-RSSEmailStack`**
(confirmed deployed in `eu-west-1`).

This costs money to keep running, duplicates CI that already lives in GitHub Actions,
and splits the build story across two systems. Everything else in the repo (lint, tests,
CDK synth checks, eval, agent workflows) is already GitHub Actions.

Facts established during exploration that shape the plan:

- The account **already has** the GitHub OIDC provider
  `arn:aws:iam::002681522526:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com`
  (used by other projects). It must be **imported**, not recreated — a duplicate fails.
- CDK bootstrap is standard, qualifier `hnb659fds`, bootstrap version 31, in `eu-west-1`.
  A deploy role therefore only needs `sts:AssumeRole` on the `cdk-hnb659fds-*` roles.
- All config parameters exist in SSM (`rss-email-AWS_ACCOUNT_ID`, `-AWS_REGION`,
  `-EMAIL_RECIPIENTS`, `-SOURCE_DOMAIN`, `-SOURCE_EMAIL_ADDRESS`, `-TO_EMAIL_ADDRESS`).
  Keeping SSM as the source of truth avoids duplicating config into GitHub secrets.
  `rss-email-FEED_DEFINITIONS_FILE` is injected by the pipeline but **is not referenced
  anywhere in `lib/rss_lambda_stack.ts`** — it is dead config and is not carried over.
- `cdk.json` currently sets `"app": "npx tsx bin/pipeline-cdk.ts"`, so `cdk deploy`
  today targets the *pipeline*, not the app.

### The one genuinely risky detail

The Stage prefix means the live stack is `cd-RSSEmailStack`, but `bin/cdk.ts` as written
would synth a stack named `RSSEmailStack`. Deploying that would **create a second,
parallel copy of every resource** (S3 bucket, CloudFront distribution, SES rule set,
Step Functions, Lambdas) instead of updating the existing one.

Fix: pin `stackName: 'cd-RSSEmailStack'` in `bin/cdk.ts`. Logical IDs inside a stack are
derived from the construct path *within* the stack, so removing the Stage wrapper does
not change any logical ID — with the stack name pinned this is a clean in-place takeover
and `cdk diff` should show no resource replacements.

---

## Approach

### 1. Repoint the CDK app at the application stack

**`bin/cdk.ts`** — make it the primary entry point:

- Fix the import to `'../lib/rss_lambda_stack.js'` (repo is `"type": "module"` with
  `moduleResolution: NodeNext`; the current extensionless import is inconsistent with
  `bin/pipeline-cdk.ts` and won't typecheck).
- Pass explicit `env: { account: process.env.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID, region: process.env.AWS_REGION }`,
  matching what `RSSPipelineAppStage` supplied, so the synthesised template stays
  environment-specific and diff-clean rather than flipping to env-agnostic pseudo-params.
- Set `stackName: 'cd-RSSEmailStack'` (see risk note above). Keep the construct id
  `'RSSEmailStack'` unchanged.

**`cdk.json`** — `"app": "npx tsx bin/cdk.ts"`.

**`package.json`** — `"synth": "tsx bin/cdk.ts"`.

**`lib/rss_lambda_stack.ts`** — one small robustness change only: line 87,
`process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` → `process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT || process.env.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID`.
Both resolve to the same account id in CI, so this produces no template diff.

*Verify:* `AWS_ACCOUNT_ID=002681522526 AWS_REGION=eu-west-1 <other env> npx cdk diff`
locally shows **no changes** (or only cosmetic metadata) against `cd-RSSEmailStack`.
This is the gate for everything downstream — do not proceed until the diff is clean.

### 2. New CDK stack for the GitHub Actions deploy role

**`lib/github_actions_role_stack.ts`** (new) + **`bin/github-oidc-cdk.ts`** (new,
separate app entry point so the role stack can never be swept into the CI deploy path).

Stack contents — an `iam.Role` named `rss-email-github-actions-deploy`:

- Trust: `iam.WebIdentityPrincipal` against the **imported** provider
  (`iam.OpenIdConnectProvider.fromOpenIdConnectProviderArn(...)`), with conditions
  `StringEquals { token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud = "sts.amazonaws.com" }` and
  `StringLike { ...:sub = "repo:eamonmason/rss-email:ref:refs/heads/main" }`.
  Scoped to `main` only, since deploy is push-to-main only.
- Permissions (deliberately minimal — the CDK bootstrap roles hold the real power):
  - `sts:AssumeRole` on `arn:aws:iam::<account>:role/cdk-hnb659fds-{deploy,file-publishing,image-publishing,lookup}-role-<account>-<region>`
  - `ssm:GetParameters` on the six `rss-email-*` config parameters
  - `ssm:GetParameter` on `/cdk-bootstrap/hnb659fds/version` (CDK CLI reads this)
- `CfnOutput` of the role ARN, for pasting into the repo variable.

Deployed once, by hand:
`npx cdk deploy --app "npx tsx bin/github-oidc-cdk.ts"`

### 3. Deploy workflow

**`.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yml`** — add `workflow_call:` to `on:` and drop
`push: branches: [main]`. It keeps running on every PR and now also runs as the gate
inside the deploy workflow, so main pushes test exactly once instead of twice.
*Caveat to accept:* the README badge will thereafter reflect PR runs only, because
reusable-workflow runs are attributed to the caller.

**`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** (new):

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
concurrency:
  group: deploy-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  test:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yml
  deploy:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps: ...
```

Deploy job steps:

1. `actions/checkout@v7`
2. `actions/setup-node@v7` with `node-version: '20'` (matches the other workflows)
3. `npm ci`
4. `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5` with
   `role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}` and `aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}`
5. **Load config from SSM** — single `aws ssm get-parameters` call for the six
   `rss-email-*` names; emit each as `::add-mask::` then append to `$GITHUB_ENV` under
   its unprefixed name (`SOURCE_DOMAIN`, `SOURCE_EMAIL_ADDRESS`, `TO_EMAIL_ADDRESS`,
   `EMAIL_RECIPIENTS`, `AWS_ACCOUNT_ID`, `AWS_REGION`). Fail the step if
   `InvalidParameters` is non-empty, rather than silently deploying with blanks —
   empty `EMAIL_RECIPIENTS` would wipe the SES receipt rule recipients.
6. `npx cdk deploy cd-RSSEmailStack --require-approval never`
   (explicit stack name; `--require-approval never` is required because the stack
   creates IAM resources). Docker is available on `ubuntu-latest`, so the Lambda layer
   uses the normal `bundlingImage` path — `CDK_DOCKER` is deliberately **not** set to
   `false` here, unlike in the lint/synth workflows.

Two repo-level **Variables** (not secrets) to create in GitHub settings:
`AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`, `AWS_REGION` (`eu-west-1`).

### 4. Remove the CodePipeline code

Delete `lib/rss_pipeline_stack.ts`, `lib/rss_pipeline_app_stage.ts`, `bin/pipeline-cdk.ts`.
Nothing else imports them (verified). `cdk.json` and `package.json` are already repointed
in step 1.

Stack teardown is left for you to run once GitHub Actions has deployed successfully:

```sh
# ⚠️ run only AFTER a green GH Actions deploy
aws cloudformation delete-stack --stack-name RSSPipelineStack --region eu-west-1
```

Destroying `RSSPipelineStack` does **not** touch `cd-RSSEmailStack` — the pipeline
created it as a separate CloudFormation stack, not a nested one. Afterwards the
CodeConnections connection
`arn:aws:codeconnections:eu-west-1:002681522526:connection/54e18fbd-fb99-4888-ac79-3a906b55f7ae`
can be deleted in the console, and the GitHub personal token secret `github-token` in
Secrets Manager is no longer needed.

### 5. Documentation

- **`README.md`** — replace "Pipeline Deployment" (lines ~487–528) with a GitHub Actions
  section: one-time role stack deploy, the two repo variables, the SSM parameters that
  remain the config source of truth, and how to trigger/watch a deploy. Update the
  "CDK Operations" block (lines ~471–485) to drop `--app "npx ts-node bin/pipeline-cdk.ts"`.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — same edits in "CDK Operations" and "Deployment"; note that
  `cdk deploy` now targets the app stack and that the deployed stack is `cd-RSSEmailStack`.
- Keep list/code-block blank-line formatting per the markdown lint rules.

---

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `bin/cdk.ts` | pin `stackName`, explicit `env`, fix `.js` import |
| `bin/github-oidc-cdk.ts` | **new** — role stack app entry |
| `lib/github_actions_role_stack.ts` | **new** — OIDC deploy role |
| `lib/rss_lambda_stack.ts` | one-line `CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` fallback |
| `cdk.json`, `package.json` | repoint app/synth to `bin/cdk.ts` |
| `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` | **new** |
| `.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yml` | `workflow_call`, drop push-on-main |
| `lib/rss_pipeline_stack.ts`, `lib/rss_pipeline_app_stage.ts`, `bin/pipeline-cdk.ts` | **delete** |
| `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | deployment docs |

---

## Verification

1. **Local synth parity (the critical check).** With the six config values exported
   from SSM, run `npx cdk diff cd-RSSEmailStack`. Expect **no resource additions,
   deletions, or replacements**. Any replacement of the S3 bucket, CloudFront
   distribution, or SES rule set means the stack-name/env pinning is wrong — stop.
2. `uv run python -m pytest tests` and
   `uv run pylint --fail-under=9.9 $(git ls-files '*.py') && uv run flake8` still pass
   (no Python changed, but the pre-commit/CI gate must stay green).
3. `CDK_DOCKER=false npx cdk synth --no-staging` succeeds with the env vars unset —
   proves `lint_and_test.yml` and `test-cdk.yml` still work now that they synth the app
   stack instead of the pipeline stack.
4. Deploy the role stack manually; confirm `aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity` is
   not needed locally, and that the CfnOutput ARN is set as `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`.
5. Open the change as a PR — confirm `Lint and Test` and `Test CDK Synth` run and pass,
   and that `deploy.yml` does **not** run on the PR.
6. Merge to main — watch the run: gate job green, OIDC assume-role succeeds, SSM step
   reports all six parameters resolved, `cdk deploy` reports
   `cd-RSSEmailStack: no changes` or a small expected change set.
7. Confirm end to end that the deployed system still works (Step Functions execution
   history / next scheduled digest), then delete `RSSPipelineStack`.

# Migrate deployment from AWS CodePipeline to GitHub Actions

## Context

Deployment today runs through a self-mutating CDK Pipeline (`RSSPipelineStack`) that
watches `eamonmason/rss-email@main` via a CodeConnections connection, synths in
CodeBuild (pulling config from SSM Parameter Store), and deploys the app stack through
a CDK Stage named `cd` — producing the CloudFormation stack **`cd-RSSEmailStack`**
(confirmed deployed in `eu-west-1`).

This costs money to keep running, duplicates CI that already lives in GitHub Actions,
and splits the build story across two systems. Everything else in the repo (lint, tests,
CDK synth checks, eval, agent workflows) is already GitHub Actions.

Facts established during exploration that shape the plan:

- The account **already has** the GitHub OIDC provider
  `arn:aws:iam::002681522526:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com`
  (used by other projects). It must be **imported**, not recreated — a duplicate fails.
- CDK bootstrap is standard, qualifier `hnb659fds`, bootstrap version 31, in `eu-west-1`.
  A deploy role therefore only needs `sts:AssumeRole` on the `cdk-hnb659fds-*` roles.
- All config parameters exist in SSM (`rss-email-AWS_ACCOUNT_ID`, `-AWS_REGION`,
  `-EMAIL_RECIPIENTS`, `-SOURCE_DOMAIN`, `-SOURCE_EMAIL_ADDRESS`, `-TO_EMAIL_ADDRESS`).
  Keeping SSM as the source of truth avoids duplicating config into GitHub secrets.
  `rss-email-FEED_DEFINITIONS_FILE` is injected by the pipeline but **is not referenced
  anywhere in `lib/rss_lambda_stack.ts`** — it is dead config and is not carried over.
- `cdk.json` currently sets `"app": "npx tsx bin/pipeline-cdk.ts"`, so `cdk deploy`
  today targets the *pipeline*, not the app.

### The one genuinely risky detail

The Stage prefix means the live stack is `cd-RSSEmailStack`, but `bin/cdk.ts` as written
would synth a stack named `RSSEmailStack`. Deploying that would **create a second,
parallel copy of every resource** (S3 bucket, CloudFront distribution, SES rule set,
Step Functions, Lambdas) instead of updating the existing one.

Fix: pin `stackName: 'cd-RSSEmailStack'` in `bin/cdk.ts`. Logical IDs inside a stack are
derived from the construct path *within* the stack, so removing the Stage wrapper does
not change any logical ID — with the stack name pinned this is a clean in-place takeover
and `cdk diff` should show no resource replacements.

---

## Approach

### 1. Repoint the CDK app at the application stack

**`bin/cdk.ts`** — make it the primary entry point:

- Fix the import to `'../lib/rss_lambda_stack.js'` (repo is `"type": "module"` with
  `moduleResolution: NodeNext`; the current extensionless import is inconsistent with
  `bin/pipeline-cdk.ts` and won't typecheck).
- Pass explicit `env: { account: process.env.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID, region: process.env.AWS_REGION }`,
  matching what `RSSPipelineAppStage` supplied, so the synthesised template stays
  environment-specific and diff-clean rather than flipping to env-agnostic pseudo-params.
- Set `stackName: 'cd-RSSEmailStack'` (see risk note above). Keep the construct id
  `'RSSEmailStack'` unchanged.

**`cdk.json`** — `"app": "npx tsx bin/cdk.ts"`.

**`package.json`** — `"synth": "tsx bin/cdk.ts"`.

**`lib/rss_lambda_stack.ts`** — one small robustness change only: line 87,
`process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT` → `process.env.CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT || process.env.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID`.
Both resolve to the same account id in CI, so this produces no template diff.

*Verify:* `AWS_ACCOUNT_ID=002681522526 AWS_REGION=eu-west-1 <other env> npx cdk diff`
locally shows **no changes** (or only cosmetic metadata) against `cd-RSSEmailStack`.
This is the gate for everything downstream — do not proceed until the diff is clean.

### 2. New CDK stack for the GitHub Actions deploy role

**`lib/github_actions_role_stack.ts`** (new) + **`bin/github-oidc-cdk.ts`** (new,
separate app entry point so the role stack can never be swept into the CI deploy path).

Stack contents — an `iam.Role` named `rss-email-github-actions-deploy`:

- Trust: `iam.WebIdentityPrincipal` against the **imported** provider
  (`iam.OpenIdConnectProvider.fromOpenIdConnectProviderArn(...)`), with conditions
  `StringEquals { token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud = "sts.amazonaws.com" }` and
  `StringLike { ...:sub = "repo:eamonmason/rss-email:ref:refs/heads/main" }`.
  Scoped to `main` only, since deploy is push-to-main only.
- Permissions (deliberately minimal — the CDK bootstrap roles hold the real power):
  - `sts:AssumeRole` on `arn:aws:iam::<account>:role/cdk-hnb659fds-{deploy,file-publishing,image-publishing,lookup}-role-<account>-<region>`
  - `ssm:GetParameters` on the six `rss-email-*` config parameters

- `CfnOutput` of the role ARN, for pasting into the repo variable.

Deployed once, by hand:
`npx cdk deploy --app "npx tsx bin/github-oidc-cdk.ts"`

### 3. Deploy workflow

**`.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yml`** — add `workflow_call:` to `on:` and drop
`push: branches: [main]`. It keeps running on every PR and now also runs as the gate
inside the deploy workflow, so main pushes test exactly once instead of twice.
*Caveat to accept:* the README badge will thereafter reflect PR runs only, because
reusable-workflow runs are attributed to the caller.

**`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** (new):

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
concurrency:
  group: deploy-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  test:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yml
  deploy:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps: ...
```

Deploy job steps:

1. `actions/checkout@v7`
2. `actions/setup-node@v7` with `node-version: '20'` (matches the other workflows)
3. `npm ci`
4. `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5` with
   `role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}` and `aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}`
5. **Load config from SSM** — single `aws ssm get-parameters` call for the six
   `rss-email-*` names; emit each as `::add-mask::` then append to `$GITHUB_ENV` under
   its unprefixed name (`SOURCE_DOMAIN`, `SOURCE_EMAIL_ADDRESS`, `TO_EMAIL_ADDRESS`,
   `EMAIL_RECIPIENTS`, `AWS_ACCOUNT_ID`, `AWS_REGION`). Fail the step if
   `InvalidParameters` is non-empty, rather than silently deploying with blanks —
   empty `EMAIL_RECIPIENTS` would wipe the SES receipt rule recipients.
6. `npx cdk deploy cd-RSSEmailStack --require-approval never`
   (explicit stack name; `--require-approval never` is required because the stack
   creates IAM resources). Docker is available on `ubuntu-latest`, so the Lambda layer
   uses the normal `bundlingImage` path — `CDK_DOCKER` is deliberately **not** set to
   `false` here, unlike in the lint/synth workflows.

`AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`, `AWS_REGION` (`eu-west-1`).

Delete `lib/rss_pipeline_stack.ts`, `lib/rss_pipeline_app_stage.ts`, `bin/pipeline-cdk.ts`.

in step 1.

```sh

aws cloudformation delete-stack --stack-name RSSPipelineStack --region eu-west-1
```

CodeConnections connection
`arn:aws:codeconnections:eu-west-1:002681522526:connection/54e18fbd-fb99-4888-ac79-3a906b55f7ae`
can be deleted in the console, and the GitHub personal token secret `github-token` in

name: Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# Never run two cdk deploys against the same stack at once. Queue instead of
# cancelling - cancelling mid-deploy would leave CloudFormation mid-update.
concurrency:
  group: deploy-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Same checks that run on every pull request, as the gate in front of deploy.
  test:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yml

  deploy:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write  # required to request the OIDC token
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Install Node.js dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v5
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
          role-session-name: rss-email-deploy-${{ github.run_id }}

      # Parameter Store stays the source of truth for deployment config - GitHub
      # holds no copies. bin/cdk.ts reads these at synth time.
      - name: Load configuration from Parameter Store
        env:
          PARAMETERS: >-
            rss-email-AWS_ACCOUNT_ID
            rss-email-AWS_REGION
            rss-email-EMAIL_RECIPIENTS
            rss-email-SOURCE_DOMAIN
            rss-email-SOURCE_EMAIL_ADDRESS
            rss-email-TO_EMAIL_ADDRESS
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          response=$(aws ssm get-parameters --names $PARAMETERS --output json)

          # Fail loudly rather than deploying with blanks - an empty
          # EMAIL_RECIPIENTS would wipe the SES receipt rule's recipient list.
          invalid=$(jq -r '.InvalidParameters | join(", ")' <<< "$response")
          if [ -n "$invalid" ]; then
            echo "::error::Missing Parameter Store parameters: $invalid"
            exit 1
          fi

          while IFS=$'\t' read -r name value; do
            key=${name#rss-email-}
            # Account id and region are not sensitive, and masking the region
            # would garble every ARN in the deploy log.
            case "$key" in
              AWS_ACCOUNT_ID|AWS_REGION) ;;
              *) echo "::add-mask::$value" ;;
            esac
            echo "$key=$value" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "Loaded $key"
          done < <(jq -r '.Parameters[] | [.Name, .Value] | @tsv' <<< "$response")

      # No CDK_DOCKER=false here, unlike the lint/synth workflows: ubuntu-latest
      # has Docker, so the Lambda layer is built in the real Python 3.13 image.
      - name: Deploy CDK stack
        run: npx cdk deploy RSSEmailStack --require-approval never

The migration is complete on the code side, and the AWS/GitHub plumbing is live.

## What changed

**CDK app repointed at the application stack**
- `cdk.json` / `package.json` now target `bin/cdk.ts` instead of `bin/pipeline-cdk.ts`
- `bin/cdk.ts` pins `stackName: 'cd-RSSEmailStack'` and sets `env` explicitly — this is what makes it an in-place takeover rather than a duplicate deployment
- `lib/rss_lambda_stack.ts`: one-line `CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT || AWS_ACCOUNT_ID` fallback

**New**
- `lib/github_actions_role_stack.ts` + `bin/github-oidc-cdk.ts` — OIDC deploy role, scoped to `refs/heads/main`, able only to assume the CDK bootstrap roles and read the six `rss-email-*` parameters
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — push-to-main, concurrency-guarded, gated on the lint/test suite, loads config from Parameter Store, `cdk deploy RSSEmailStack`

**Removed**: `lib/rss_pipeline_stack.ts`, `lib/rss_pipeline_app_stage.ts`, `bin/pipeline-cdk.ts`

**Docs**: README and CLAUDE.md deployment sections rewritten.

## Verification

- **`cdk diff` against the live stack**: resolved to `Stack RSSEmailStack (cd-RSSEmailStack)`, no replacement of the bucket, SES rule set, Step Functions, IAM role, or CloudFront distribution. Two cosmetic changes are unavoidable — CDK's app-root-relative `uniqueId` appears in a Lambda permission's logical ID and in the CloudFront origin `Id`/OAI comment, so both get recreated/renamed in place. Neither is destructive.
- 175 tests pass; pylint 9.98; flake8 clean; synth succeeds both with and without env vars set (the two CI paths).
- OIDC role stack deployed: `arn:aws:iam::002681522526:role/rss-email-github-actions-deploy`; repo variables `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` and `AWS_REGION` set.

Two things I did **not** do, per your earlier choices: the work is uncommitted on branch `migrate-to-github-actions-deploy`, and `RSSPipelineStack` is still deployed — delete it (plus the CodeConnections connection and the `github-token` Secrets Manager secret) once a GitHub Actions deploy has gone green.

One side fix worth flagging: `cdk.out` wasn't excluded from flake8, so `uv run flake8` returned hundreds of warnings from vendored dependencies after any synth. Added to `setup.cfg`.

A caveat on `lint_and_test.yml`: dropping its `push: [main]` trigger means its status badge will now reflect PR runs only, since reusable-workflow runs are attributed to the caller. Separately, `tsc --noEmit` fails repo-wide (missing `@types/node` wiring in `tsconfig.json`) — pre-existing, went from 22 errors to 20, and no workflow runs it.

ci: migrate deployment from CodePipeline to GitHub Actions

Replace the self-mutating CDK Pipeline (RSSPipelineStack) with a
push-to-main GitHub Actions workflow that authenticates via OIDC.

The CDK app now points at bin/cdk.ts rather than bin/pipeline-cdk.ts.
The stack name is pinned to 'cd-RSSEmailStack' because the pipeline
deployed it through a Stage named 'cd', which prefixed the name -
without the pin, deploying would create a parallel copy of every
resource rather than updating the existing stack. Verified with
cdk diff: no resource replacements.

Parameter Store remains the single source of truth for deployment
config; the workflow reads the rss-email-* parameters at deploy time
so no copies live in GitHub. The deploy role can do nothing but
assume the CDK bootstrap roles and read those parameters, and is
scoped to refs/heads/main of this repository.

lint_and_test.yml becomes a reusable workflow called as the deploy
gate, so pushes to main run the checks once rather than twice.

Also exclude cdk.out from flake8 and pylint, which otherwise report
hundreds of warnings from bundled dependencies after a synth.
